links.outcome: Test-retest reproducibility of LI-RADS scores across five repeated runs (ICC), structured vs free-text
links.effect: Test-retest reliability ICC was 0.81 for free-text vs 0.50 for structured reports on 50 lesions passed five times.
links.quote: the test-retest reliability was higher (ICC = 0.81 vs. 0.50), in free-text compared to structured reports, respectively

links.outcome: Accuracy of LI-RADS classification by GPT-3.5 against radiologist consensus ground truth
links.effect: Accuracy was 53% on unstructured and 44% on structured reports; kappa 0.51 and 0.44.
links.quote: The accuracy of ChatGPT at determining LI-RADS categories was poor (53% and 44% on unstructured and structured reports).

screen.reason: Evaluates ChatGPT's capability and test-retest reliability in assigning LI-RADS scores from German radiology reports without testing a deployment safeguard or organizational practice.
